Stated Claim / Post Context:
Affordability: Rent Prices Down 13 Percent After Trump Closes Border

President Donald Trump's immigration reforms have reduced average after-inflation rents by 13 percent below the height of President Joe Biden's mass-migration policy.
The post Affordability: Rent Prices Down 13 Percent After Trump Closes Border appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump’s immigration reforms have reduced average after-inflation rents by 13 percent below the height of President Joe Biden’s mass-migration policy.

Average rents jumped to $1,774 in the summer of 2022 and then fell to $1,694 in September 2026, according to rental data from Realtor.com. That is an $80 monthly cut, or $960 a year.

But the cut is larger because post-2022 inflation should have jacked up the 2022 rent to $1,953 in 2026. Once that inflation impact is counted, the rent rollback is roughly $259 per month, or 13 percent below prices in Biden’s unaffordable migration summer.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other deputies have noted the gains for American citizens.

But President Donald Trump’s White House has said little about the gains for renters — likely because Trump is acting as a cheerleader for nervous real estate investors and landlords who lose revenue when migrants are sent home.

The real estate professionals are nervous because the stock value of rental properties has dropped, partly because Trump has reduced the migrant population. For example, in 2021, the Multi-Family Real Estate Apartment Price Index gained $108 billion. That spike created a “record high [of] $412.80 billion (June 2022); the latest level [June 2026] is 22.9% below it,” Macrotrends.net reported in June 2026.

In 2027, Democrat progressives will gain power in Congress, and they are joining hands with real estate lobbyists to demand yet more migration via many asylum and visa channels. The push is being wrapped in the Democrats’ affordability mantra — even though it would shove tens of millions of Americans back to the days of unaffordable Biden rents.

Biden’s Migration

For consumers, the decline in rents since 2022 is masked by the monthly interplay of inflation and wages, which have kept after-inflation wages largely flat under Trump after four years of decline under Biden.

Biden’s decision to open the border in 2021 invited millions of migrants into Americans’ apartment housing.

His economics team expected the low-wage migrants to offset the inflation created by his massive Bidenomics spending plan. But they missed migrants’ massive impact on rental prices, which then bumped up Biden’s high inflation rate.

The sudden rush in renter demand — roughly 1.5 million new migrant rentals — caused an immediate spike in rental costs that peaked in 2022, despite the economic meltdown caused in 2020 and 2021 by the coronavirus.
